gameplay_checks.scope: Original legacy actor outcomes retained; valid capture bytes do not turn failed gameplay into passing evidence

source_binding.limit: Actual native actor, callback frames and original PCM bytes rechecked. No mixer stop clock, public movie, playback, audition or fresh build is claimed.

capture_timebase: Legacy audio_seconds is screenshot callback CPU time relative to StartRecordingOutput; audio-render clock offset is unmeasured. world_seconds is fixture elapsed gameplay time.
phase_timebase_limit: Original native labels preserved; chapter edges use first observed callback of each phase, not exact operation times.

measurement_limits: This analyzer performs no perceptual audition or playback.
Sample peaks are not oversampled true peaks, LUFS, or a guarantee against intersample clipping.
Full-scale sample counts use signed PCM endpoint values; near-full-scale counts use -0.1 dBFS.
Silence uses the maximum absolute channel sample per frame at the configured threshold; exact-zero counts are separate.
Energy events group RMS-threshold windows with the configured merge gap; they are not verified shot or animation event counts.
Phase labels are supplied capture annotations; no automatic identification of weapon type or event synchrony is claimed.
Null dBFS means exactly zero measured amplitude, mathematically negative infinity.
measurements.near_clip_window_limit: Each listed 100 ms window contains at least one sample at or above -0.1 dBFS; boundaries are window quantization, not exact clip duration. All signed PCM endpoints are counted separately.
measurements.phase_energy_policy: Zero-energy phases are measured, never automatically failed; pause/death and intentionally quiet intervals require context. Threshold bursts are not inferred shots, contacts, voices or exact animation markers.

limits: Every original integer PCM sample contributes to peak/RMS/full-scale counts; no warmup, quiet phase or loud spike is excluded.
Sample peaks are not true peak or LUFS. Numerical energy does not establish timbre, spatial localization, realism, event synchronization or user approval.
Phase boundaries use first observed frame timestamps. CPU/audio-render clock offset is not measured or corrected.
